newsitem.title: GREECE: SOCCER-SUKER GOAL PUTS CROATIA BACK IN WORLD CUP RACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUKER GOAL PUTS CROATIA BACK IN WORLD CUP RACE.

text.p: Croatia stayed on course for a place in the World Cup finals on Wednesday beating Greece 1-0 with a away win in group one, sealed by Real Madrid's top scorer Davor Suker.
Suker put an end to string of near misses by the Croats in the 74th minute when he drove home from inside the box after a perfect pass from West Ham defender Slaven Bilic.
The Croats braved heavy rain and stayed in control throughout the match with Suker, Seville's Robert Prosinecki and Milan's Svonimir Boban often spreading panic in the Greek defence.
Prosineki shot slightly wide from 20 metres in the 16th and 30th minutes and Boban hit the woodwork from six metres in the 72nd.
"We are back in the race," said Croat coach Miroslav Balazevic after his side had drawn their last three matches.
"We were playing our last card in Greece and played very well. I am very happy for this victory against a strong team like Greece."
The Croats had only six points from four matches before the game and badly needed the win. They are now on nine points, one point behind Denmark and Greece, each with 10 points.
The hosts came close to scoring in the 23rd when Croat goalkeeper Drazen Ladic saved a fierce header from Theodore Zagorakis after a corner.
They had another chance in the 70th when Backburn Rovers' George Donis failed to push the ball inside the net after a mixup in the Croat defence.
Demis Nikolaidis, Greece's best striker, was replaced in the 13th minute with a thigh injury.
"The fight in group one is now back to square one," Greek coach Costas Polychroniou said. "We will fight for a ticket to the finals until the end.
